https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.name: Ecological Audit
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.dataSource: 20,000 real de-identified opt-in Ash user conversations (10,000 September 2025, 10,000 December 2025) with a minimum of three messages each covering naturalistic suicidal ideation and non-suicidal self-injury disclosures.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.groundTruth: Licensed clinical psychologist labels for whether SI/NSSI was present and whether crisis resources were delivered, from two reviewers with a third adjudicating (97% agreement, 332/343), plus a blinded 600-conversation random sample reviewed independently.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.evaluation: An LLM judge calibrated against licensed clinical psychologist ratings was run four times per session and scored each conversation binary (flag/no flag) for SI/NSSI against a detailed clinician-authored rubric distinguishing genuine ideation from situational distress, metaphor, and past history; flagged sessions missed by the production classifier went to clinician review, with the primary metric being end-to-end failure rate.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.population: Real chatbot users using a deployed mental health chatbot

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.name: CAPE-II
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.dataSource: Trained raters role-played youth personas with mental-health challenges based on description that fucntion as dynamic scripts.
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.groundTruth: Ground truth based on qualitative assessment of LLM responses using CAPE-II rubric (9 sections, binary high-quality ratings)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.evaluation: Human: trained raters apply CAPE-II; proportion of high-quality ratings compared across chatbots (Bonferroni-corrected chi-square)

https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.name: eConsult-Templates
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.dataSource: 145 expert-crafted clinical consultation templates developed and routinely used by Stanford's eConsult team (general specialties, not mental-health-specific)
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.groundTruth: the expert-crafted eConsult templates as reference
https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PM.evaluation: Comparison of LLM-generated templates against the expert reference templates using semantic autograder (OpenAI o3). Autograder was claibrated first using 40 templates grading GPT-4.1 or o3 which was reviewed by 3 blinded US board-certified internal medicine physicians.

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32401222.name: PostRisk
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32401222.dataSource: 1,588 forum posts from the CLPsych 2017 shared task (Reachout.com), labeled for perceived suicide risk / moderator attention
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32401222.groundTruth: CLPsych moderator/risk labels for 200 posts developed by 3 judges who discussed and came to shared aggreement for 200 posts and annotating remaining posts which were compared for interannotator aggreement (excluding 22 posts).
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32401222.evaluation: Automated triage classification comparing text-representation methods (lexicon tools, DeepMoji, Universal Sentence Encoder, GPT-1) via AutoML (TPOT, Auto-Sklearn)

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.name: SOS-HL-1K (Suicidal Risk)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.dataSource: 1,249 Chinese social-media posts keyword-filtered on depression/suicide/despair and manually cleaned of encouraging posts, ads, and emoji-only comments by non-clinician study team
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.groundTruth: Binary high/low suicide risk labels from three annotators with clinical psychology or counseling backgrounds, trained on a shared guide, with a senior licensed psychologist arbitrating disagreements.
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.population: Anonymous Chinese Weibo users posting to a public suicide-related memorial blog between 2017 to 2019

https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.name: SocialCD-3K (Cognitive Distortion)
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.dataSource: 3,407 Chinese social-media posts for multi-label cognitive-distortion detection, manually cleaned of encouraging posts, ads, and emoji-only comments by non-clinician study team
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.groundTruth: Multi-label cognitive distortion annotations from three clinically trained annotators, with senior psychologist arbitrating disagreements
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40868395.population: Anonymous Chinese Weibo users posting to a public suicide-related memorial blog between 2017 to 2019

https://www.nature.com/articles/s44277-0.name: Conversational Benchmarks
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44277-0.dataSource: Prompts written by registered public contributors describing a person in distress, tagged to five domains — suicide, self-harm, eating disorders, grief, and psychosis — with finer subtags such as imminent suicide crisis and body image. Each prompt is paired with a candidate supportive response; the current snapshot covers 500 prompt-response pairs, and the set grows continuously as contributions come in.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44277-0.groundTruth: The mean appropriateness rating given by public raters on a −3 to +3 scale, roughly 15 raters per response. Rater qualifications are not stated on the site, and the platform treats the spread of ratings as meaningful rather than collapsing to a single correct answer.
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44277-0.evaluation: Models rate each response on the same −3 to +3 scale and are compared to the human mean
https://www.nature.com/articles/s44277-0.population: Simulated help-seeker population (scenarios written by community contributors, not drawn from real help-seeking exchanges)

https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12871.name: MentalBench
https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12871.dataSource: 24,750 synthetic clinical cases generated from MentalKG, a DSM-5 knowledge graph of diagnostic criteria and differential diagnosis rules for 23 disorders, built and validated by two experts. Seeds sample from graph, augmented with symptom subtypes and demographic profiles, then written into narratives by three LLMs. Four case types: chart-style complete summaries (1,725), fragmented first-person self-reports (3,450), ambiguous differential pairs with discriminating evidence omitted (6,525), and the same pairs with it included (13,050).
https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12871.groundTruth: Answer key: the diagnosis / two-diagnosis set entailed by MentalKG logic presented as 4 options with distractors chosen by symptomatic overlap. Options and labels designed by domain experts and reviewed case by case.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12871.evaluation: Automated match against accuracy, correct only if full answer set returned. Errors classified as over-diagnosis, under-diagnosis, or incorrect.

https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01329.name: PsyCrisisBench
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01329.dataSource: 540 real hotline call transcripts from the Hangzhou Psychological Assistance Hotline, drawn from 21,527 calls in 2023 after excluding invalid, information-only, and repeat calls; 270 high-risk calls plus 270 non-high-risk controls matched on call time, gender, marital status, and call type. Audio transcribed with Whisper into turn-by-turn dialogue, errors and filler words left in. A separate 520 calls from 2022 supply few-shot examples and fine-tuning data. Each transcript run 3 times per model.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01329.groundTruth: Four binary labels per call — mood status, suicidal ideation, suicide plan, and risk level — recorded by hotline operators trained in suicide risk assessment in structured post-call annotations. Labels were produced during service delivery, not for the study; no inter-rater reliability or adjudication reported.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01329.evaluation: Automated accuracy against operator-assigned labels, averaged over 3 runs and reported per task.
https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.01329.population: Callers to a public psych support hotline in China, 2023
